selected_experts.reason: Verify the fish's identity as a tench (Tinca tinca) by checking for key taxonomic features: small deeply embedded cycloid scales, olive-green to golden-bronze coloration, small head with blunt downturned mouth, two short barbels at each corner of the mouth, small eyes with reddish-orange iris, short rounded dorsal fin, truncate to slightly emarginate caudal fin, and a complete lateral line.

Locate the tench in the image to ensure it is properly segmented and distinguishable from the background and the person holding it. This is crucial for subsequent detailed analysis of the fish's features.

Check the boundaries of the tench to ensure it is a single, continuous physical entity without floating parts or blurred edges. Verify that the fins are properly attached and not fused with the body or background.

Assess the overall image quality, focusing on the texture of the fish's skin to ensure it appears mucous-coated and smooth, as characteristic of a tench. Check for any texture blur or compression artifacts that might obscure these details.

Verify the spatial relationship between the person and the tench. Ensure the fish is being held naturally and that there is no perspective distortion or spatial bleeding between the person's hands and the fish.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay special attention to the presence and structure of the barbels at the corners of the mouth, the texture and embedding of the scales, the shape and ray count of the dorsal and caudal fins, and the visibility of the lateral line. Ensure the fish's coloration matches the typical olive-green to golden-bronze dorsal and pale yellow-white ventral pattern. Verify that the person holding the fish is depicted naturally without any anatomical distortions or spatial inconsistencies.
